verdict.reasoning: Patient reports dry, itchy skin on arms and hands and redness: "I've got, really dry itchy skin" and "All over my arms, um, and my hands mainly" and "my skin's quite red"; onset "I think it started a few days ago."

Onset after swimming and no prior episodes: "I went swimming a few days ago" and "did your symptoms start after you went swimming?" Patient: "Uh, yes"; earlier: "is this something you've had before?" Patient: "Uh, no. Never had".
Coconut butter ineffective: Patient says, "I'm using coconut butter for the past few days" and doctor asks "the coconut butter hasn't helped, with the itch?" Patient responds "No".

Transcript supports no spots, fever, sweating, vomiting, loose stools, or urinary problems, and no bleeding/discharge, but does NOT mention cracks or pruritic skin discharge: "I don't have any spots, and no fever, and I'm not sweating either"; "No" to vomiting/loose stools and urine issues; doctor: "no bleeding or discharge from skin"; there is no statement about absence of cracked skin (only a question "have you noticed any cracked skin?") so asserting 'no cracks' adds unsupported detail.
Patient reports tiredness: Doctor asks, "do you feel generally run-down? Do you feel tired?" Patient: "Uh, yeah, I think I have been, quite tired."
Normal eating and drinking: Doctor asks, "Are you eating and drinking OK?" Patient: "Yeah, I've been drinking, and eating as normal."

No past skin problems or other conditions mentioned: Doctor asks about prior skin problems "things like eczema or, um, dermatitis?" Patient: "Uh, no"; no other past medical conditions are reported in the history.
Medication list includes Microgynon: Patient says, "I'm currently taking"; doctor clarifies "Microgynon" and explains it is "a contraceptive pill"; patient agrees "Yeah."
Possible lactose intolerance: Doctor asks about allergies; patient: "I think, um, I might be lactose intolerant."
Father's asthma: Patient states, "my dad has asthma."
Mother's hayfever: Patient states, "my mum has hayfever."
Lives alone: Doctor asks, "who do you live with at home?" Patient: "Ohh, it's just me." Doctor confirms, "Live alone?" Patient: "Yep."
Non-smoker and minimal alcohol: Doctor: "Do you smoke... Are you a smoker?" Patient: "Uh, no, I don't smoke." Doctor: "Do you drink much in the way of alcohol?" Patient: "Uh, no."
Denies drug use: Doctor asks, "Recreational drugs?" Patient: "No."

Works as primary school teacher, stressed, long hours: Patient: "I work as a teacher" and later confirmed as primary school: "you work as a primary school teacher?" Patient: "Yes, that's right." Stress and long hours: "I've been really stressed at work" and "I've been working really long hours."

Doctor suspects dermatitis likely related to swimming exposure (irritant/contact): "you've got a dry itchy rash on your, mainly your hands... and your arms which started, perhaps after swimming a few days ago" and "I wonder whether you may have something called dermatitis." This supports a likely contact/irritant dermatitis after swimming.

Assessment includes stress and fatigue: Work stress and tiredness are documented: "I've been really stressed at work" and to "do you feel tired?" patient: "yeah... quite tired"; doctor notes stress can be a contributing factor to symptoms.
Dermatitis leaflet offered: Doctor says, "Well I can give you a patient information leaflet about that, which gives a bit more information about the disease."
Topical steroid cream: Doctor: "we have steroid creams I can give you, um, which will help with the inflammation."

Use emollients multiple times daily: Doctor: "something called emollients, which can help with the dry, dry skin. And that's something you just need to kind of paste on, uh, on to your skin... throughout the day for the next few days."
OTC antihistamines for itch: Doctor: "you can also try antihistamines, so you can get things over the counter, Piriton, Loratadine, they can sometimes help with the itchiness."
Follow-up in about a week if not better: Doctor: "if it's still not getting better, come back and see me next week, and we can have another look again, at your symptoms."
